system_overview: This specification is a modified version of the spanning tree algorithm in which the edge set is not a declared constant but is instead a state variable that is initialized to any possible set of edges with nodes from the node set. This allows the model checker to exhaustively test the spanning tree algorithm on all possible undirected graphs having a particular number of nodes, verifying correctness for every graph topology.
actors_and_components: The system operates on an undirected graph with a fixed set of nodes. The edge set is a variable that can take on any valid graph structure. There is a single designated root node. The algorithm is the same centralized spanning tree algorithm as the base module.
state_variables: The system maintains three state components: (1) a parent function that maps each node to its parent in the spanning tree, (2) a distance function that maps each node to a natural number representing its computed distance from the root, and (3) an edge set variable that holds the graph structure (initialized nondeterministically and then held constant throughout execution).
initial_state: Every node's parent is set to itself. The root node's distance is set to 0. All other nodes' distances are set to the maximum cardinality constant. The edge set is chosen nondeterministically from all possible sets of two-element subsets of the node set, representing every possible undirected graph (without self-loops) on those nodes.
actions: Same as the base spanning tree algorithm: choose a node and one of its graph neighbors such that the neighbor's distance plus one is strictly less than the node's current distance. Choose a new distance for the node that is strictly less than its current distance but at least the neighbor's distance plus one. Update the node's distance and parent accordingly. The edge set remains unchanged during all transitions.
safety_properties: When the algorithm terminates, the postcondition holds for every possible graph: for every node, one of three cases applies: (1) it is the root with distance 0 and parent equal to itself; (2) it is unreachable with maximum distance, parent equal to itself, and all neighbors also unreachable; or (3) it has a distance between 1 and the maximum minus one, its parent is a graph neighbor, and its distance equals its parent's distance plus one. The safety property asserts this postcondition holds upon termination.
liveness_properties: The postcondition is eventually reached. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
model_bounds: The set of nodes, the root node, and the maximum cardinality constant are declared as constants. Testing with 4 nodes takes a few seconds. Testing with 5 nodes takes about 25 minutes. Testing with 6 nodes will likely exhaust available memory, because computing the initial edge set requires enumerating all subsets of all subsets of the node set, which for N nodes contains 2 to the power of 2 to the N elements.
additional_assumptions: The root must be a member of the node set. The maximum cardinality must be a natural number at least as large as the number of nodes. The edge set variable is initialized nondeterministically but never changes after initialization, effectively acting as a universally quantified constant. This module uses randomization support for the nondeterministic initial state generation.
